subject: physics_2
question_text: Explain series combination of capacitors. Derive the formula for equivalent capacitance in each combination.

verification.note: The 1+2+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Two structural checks are IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the two-book union check (the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only) and the past-paper back-test (the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers). Hand-checked: in series Q is common, V = V₁+V₂+V₃ with Vᵢ = Q/Cᵢ gives 1/C = 1/C₁+1/C₂+1/C₃ — the book's chain, correct. The question text is the book's, including its 'in each combination' tail (this card derives the series case; the parallel case is its own SAQ).

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The arrangement
lines: In series, the second plate of the first
capacitor joins the first plate of the second,
and so on down the line. The two free end
plates join the two battery terminals.
The same charge Q appears on each capacitor;
the applied V is shared between them.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Plate-to-plate in one line; same Q on each, V shared.
steps.why: The plate pair joining two neighbours is an isolated conductor — charge separating on one face must come from the other — so one Q runs through the whole chain, and the battery's V is split across the gaps.
common_mistakes: Saying V is the same on each — in series it is the CHARGE that is common.
Describing plates joined to common terminals — that is the parallel arrangement.

recall.must_convey: That capacitors join plate to plate in one line, the same Q sits on each, and V is shared.
accept: plate to plate in a line
reject: one by C is the sum of one by C i

steps.memory_tip: Series: one path, one Q, shared V.

steps.label: The figure
steps.margin_note: Three capacitors in one line across the battery V.
steps.why: One unbroken path through all three gaps is what makes the same Q appear on each capacitor — the figure shows there is nowhere else for the charge to go.
common_mistakes: Drawing the capacitors in separate branches — that is the parallel figure.

recall.must_convey: That three capacitors are drawn in one line with a battery across the ends.
reject: V is V one plus V two plus V three

steps.memory_tip: One wire, three gaps, one battery below.

steps.label: Adding the potential differences
lines: The applied potential difference is the sum
With the common charge Q on each capacitor,

lines.text: V₁ = Q/C₁, V₂ = Q/C₂, V₃ = Q/C₃

lines: If C is the equivalent capacitance, V = Q/C:
steps.margin_note: Two marks. V adds; each Vᵢ is the same Q over its own Cᵢ.
steps.why: The equivalent capacitor is DEFINED as the one that draws the same Q at the same total V — writing V = Q/C beside the sum is what turns the physics into the formula.
common_mistakes: Adding charges instead of potential differences — charges are all equal here.
Using different charges Q₁, Q₂, Q₃ — series forces one common Q.

recall.must_convey: That V is the sum of the three potential differences, each equal to Q over its own C.
accept: V is V one plus V two plus V three
each V is Q by its C
reject: plate to plate in a line

steps.memory_tip: Series: the V's add up, the Q factors out.

steps.label: The equivalent capacitance
lines: The equivalent C is smaller than the smallest
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Box the reciprocal sum and note that C comes out smaller.
steps.why: Adding gaps in series is like lengthening the gap of one capacitor — harder to store charge — so reciprocals add and the result is smaller than every member.
common_mistakes: Writing C = C₁ + C₂ + C₃ — that is the parallel formula.
Forgetting that the reciprocal sum still needs inverting to get C itself.

recall.must_convey: That one by C equals the sum of the three reciprocals, and C is smaller than the smallest.
accept: one by C is the sum of one by C i
reject: C is C one plus C two plus C three

steps.memory_tip: Series capacitors behave like parallel resistors: reciprocals add.

insider_note: The one line that earns the middle marks is V₁ = Q/C₁ etc. with the SAME Q — the examiner checks that no Q₁, Q₂, Q₃ appear.
